audit.why: Even lane (51.31% WR, 3120 games). Early is Malzahar-favoured (Veigar has no waveclear pre-stacks), mid is Malzahar's kill window (point-click R beats skillshot setup), late flips to a stacked Veigar. Content layer already states this correctly.

Spikes: Lost Chapter shove engine (4-5), level 6 point-click suppress window, Liandry's first item, late flip when Veigar's AP stacks make R a missing-health execute. spikes[0..3] cover all four accurately.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns has no digit; full-layer level chart contradicts content win[] on 6 of 7 rows; enemyWin is a lane-agnostic template.
audit.why: Event Horizon is 20s rank 1 / 14s max — the longest, most punishable cooldown in his kit and the gate on his whole combo. Veigar R 120/90/60 vs Malzahar R 140/110/80. Malzahar Q silence denies his casts; his cage stuns only on the edge. Content whys are kit-grounded; full sides were left on a stale template.
audit.corrected: Cooldown numbers added; full phases[].side aligned to content win[] with rewritten whys; enemyWin grounded in cage-edge-stun into Dark Matter + missing-health R.

edits.before: E a caster minion and let the visions farm for you — your lane is a macro pattern, not a duel, from the first wave.
edits.after: E the wave and shove: he has no waveclear before his Q stacks build, so you win level 1 outright and deny his early farm.

edits.before: Q online: the silence is your trade answer. Use it on his engage spell, not on poke he can walk around.
edits.after: His cage comes online and evens it — your silence answers his setup, but a landed Event Horizon answers you back.

edits.before: W voidlings turn your shove permanent — the wave hits his tower while you ward, roam-shadow, or just exist safely.
edits.after: Still even: he farms Baleful Strike stacks safely while your voidlings shove — neither side can force without risk.

edits.before: Lost Chapter and the machine is complete: E-hops fund themselves, the wave is always crashing, and his tower is always bleeding.
edits.after: Lost Chapter completes the shove engine, and your point-click threat beats his skillshot setup — you edge ahead through 4-5.

edits.before: Liandry's spike: visions melt waves AND health bars. Suppress-into-burn kills through most defensive answers.
edits.after: Liandry's spike: you out-push and threaten suppress on every step-up; suppress-into-burn kills through his answers.

edits.before: Late Malz is a number: one suppression on their carry equals one won teamfight. Shield up, flank smart, press R.
edits.after: Stacked Veigar flips it: infinite AP, an execute R, and a cage that locks your stationary channel — dodge the edge or die.

edits.before: - Veigar Event Horizon (Cage): matchup-defining — Only the cage EDGE stuns — hold position near the center or leave before it forms; never dash into the wall. It governs your forward steps. - spell shield (Iron Boundary) spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Veigar Event Horizon (Cage): 20s at rank 1, 14s max — only the EDGE stuns, so hold near the center or leave before it forms; it governs every forward step. - His R is 120/90/60s to your 140/110/80 — trade ults evenly. - A spell shield spent on poke is a death you scheduled.

edits.before: Pop-and-punish: poke his shield off with a cheap E-tick, then Q-W-E the gap before it rebuilds — full rotations only ever land on shieldless targets.
edits.after: Call of the Void's silence interrupts his wind-up — hold it for the moment he steps up to cast Event Horizon, and his whole combo never gets to start.

edits.before: Trading into him with YOUR shield down — you are the squishiest scaling mage in the pool the moment the purple bubble disappears.
edits.after: Q after Dark Matter already landed silences nothing — his W is near-zero cooldown when stacked, so deny the NEXT cage, not the last hit.

edits.before: Flash + Teleport standard — TP doubles your shove-tax map game. Ghost-cleanse setups exist into hard dive; Ignite pairs with R kill threats if you want lane blood.
edits.after: Flash + Teleport standard — TP turns each wave crash into a cross-map play. Ghost-Cleanse exists into hard dive; Ignite pairs with R kill threats if you want lane blood.

edits.before: Veigar wins by landing Event Horizon (Cage), denying your pattern, and keeping the fight at a distance your kit resents.
edits.after: Veigar wins by caging your channel — Event Horizon's edge stun into Dark Matter and a missing-health Primordial Burst deletes you.
